oneLiner: 组建—震荡—规范—执行:新团队几乎都要先经历摩擦,才谈得上高效。
oneLinerEn: Forming, storming, norming, performing — new teams mostly pass through friction before they flow.
detail: 布鲁斯·塔克曼(1965)描述团队:组建期礼貌试探,震荡期因角色与分歧而冲突,规范期建立默契与规则,执行期才能真正协同发力(后来又加“解散期”)。启示是把早期冲突看作正常必经,而非团队失败的信号;领导者在各阶段要换支持方式。
detailEn: Bruce Tuckman (1965): forming is polite probing, storming clashes over roles and views, norming builds shared rules, performing finally delivers (adjourning was added later). Treat early conflict as a normal stage, not failure, and change how you support the team at each one.

oneLiner: 敢说话、敢认错、敢提不同意见而不怕被羞辱——高效团队的第一预测指标。
oneLinerEn: Speaking up, admitting error, dissenting without fear of humiliation — the top predictor of effective teams.
detail: 艾米·埃德蒙森研究发现:最好的团队不是没有错误,而是敢于把错误摆上桌讨论,因此学习更快。心理安全不等于降低标准或一团和气,而是“相互尊重 + 直言不讳”。它也是谷歌“亚里士多德计划”对高效团队影响最大的因素。
detailEn: Amy Edmondson found the best teams are not error-free but bold enough to put errors on the table, so they learn faster. Psychological safety is not lowered standards or false harmony but mutual respect plus candour — and it topped Google's Project Aristotle as the strongest factor in effective teams.

oneLiner: 看得见的器物、信奉的价值观、潜意识的基本假设——文化由表及里三层。
oneLinerEn: Artefacts you see, espoused values you claim, and taken-for-granted assumptions — culture in three depths.
detail: 埃德加·沙因把组织文化分:最外层是能观察的器物(布局、仪式、口号),中间是公开宣称的价值观,最深是未被言明、被视为理所当然的基本假设。真正的文化在最深层,这也解释了为何墙上的标语改不动行为——变革要触及那些没说出口的假设。
detailEn: Edgar Schein split it into artefacts you can observe, espoused values, and the deepest unspoken, taken-for-granted assumptions. Real culture lives at the bottom — which is why wall slogans fail to change behaviour: to shift culture you must reach the assumptions no one says aloud.

oneLiner: 从制造紧迫感到巩固成果:变革失败常败在第一步“够不够急”和跳过中段沟通。
oneLinerEn: From seeding urgency to anchoring gains — change usually fails on step one and on skipping the middle.
detail: 约翰·科特(1996)八步:营造紧迫感、组建领导联盟、构建愿景、沟通变革、授权行动、创造短期胜利、乘胜推进、把新做法融入文化。他强调多数失败源于自满与沟通不足,而非计划错误;八步是顺序逻辑,跳步会让变革停在表面。
detailEn: John Kotter's eight steps (1996): urgency, a guiding coalition, a vision, communication, empowerment, short-term wins, consolidation and anchoring in culture. He held most failures come from complacency and under-communication, not bad plans — and the steps are sequential; skipping leaves change skin-deep.

oneLiner: 组织变革最终发生在每个人身上:认知—渴望—知识—能力—巩固。
oneLinerEn: Organisational change happens one person at a time: Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement.
detail: 普罗赛提出:变革卡住,往往能定位到 A-D-K-A-R 某一环——员工不知道为何要变、不想变、不会变、做不到或没人强化维持。它把宏大的“推行变革”拆成可诊断的个人旅程,便于对症下药,而不是一刀切地发通知、办培训。
detailEn: Prosci's model says a stalled change can be traced to one letter — people unaware why, unwilling, lacking knowledge, unable, or unreinforced. It breaks a grand roll-out into a diagnosable individual journey you can treat point by point rather than one broadcast and one training.

oneLiner: 按“坚持自己 / 顾及对方”两维,人有竞争、协作、妥协、回避、迁就五种反应。
oneLinerEn: On the axes of assertiveness and cooperativeness sit five responses: competing, collaborating, compromising, avoiding, accommodating.
detail: 托马斯与基尔曼用关心自己与关心他人两轴画出五种风格,没有一种永远最好:紧迫重大议题可能要竞争,双赢且关系重要时该协作,临时分歧用妥协,琐碎或情绪上头时回避或迁就各有其用。认清自己惯用的那一把,再按情境换。
detailEn: Thomas and Kilmann map five styles on two axes — concern for self and for others. None is always best: compete when the issue is vital and time short, collaborate for genuine win-win, compromise on temporary splits, avoid or accommodate for trivial or heated moments. Know your default and switch by situation.

oneLiner: 目标—反馈—评估—发展闭环;一年一度的打分正被持续对话取代。
oneLinerEn: A loop of goals, feedback, appraisal and development — the annual rating gives way to ongoing conversation.
detail: 考核要衡量成果与行为、对齐目标(承接 MBO/OKR)、并服务于发展与激励而非只定薪酬。常见问题是各类认知偏差:近因效应、光环效应、宽大化、以及被“绩效焦虑”扭曲。趋势是把一年一次的评判拆成频繁的目标校准与教练式反馈。
detailEn: Appraisal should weigh results and behaviour, align to goals (the MBO/OKR lineage) and serve growth and motivation, not set pay alone. Its flaws are cognitive: recency, halo, leniency and distortion by rating pressure. The drift is from a yearly verdict to frequent goal-setting and coaching feedback.

oneLiner: 法定、奖赏、强制、专家、参照——影响力可来自职位,也可来自能力与人格。
oneLinerEn: Legitimate, reward, coercive, expert and referent — influence can come from the chair, or from skill and character.
detail: 弗伦奇与雷文(1959)指出权力不止是职位授权:专家权力(懂得多)与参照权力(让人信服愿追随)往往比奖惩、强制更持久、更少抵触。管理者若只有“法定权力”而缺专业与信任,指令会打折;真正的权威多为后者。
detailEn: French and Raven (1959) showed power is more than the office: expert power (knowing more) and referent power (being trusted and followed) usually outlast and draw less resistance than reward or coercion. A manager with only legitimate power but little expertise or trust finds commands discounted; lasting authority leans on the latter.

term: 勒温变革:解冻—变革—再冻结
oneLiner: 先打破旧平衡(解冻),再推行新做法(变革),最后固化为新的常态(再冻结)。
oneLinerEn: Break the old equilibrium (unfreeze), move to the new (change), then lock it in as the new normal (refreeze).
detail: 库尔特·勒温用场论把变革看作“力场”中驱动与抑制力量的博弈:不先让人意识到旧方式行不通,新方式就难以落地;改变了若不强化、不纳入制度与文化,就会回弹。这三步是后来许多变革模型(含科特八步)的骨架。
detailEn: Kurt Lewin saw change as a force field of driving and restraining powers: unless people feel the old way no longer works, the new one will not land, and unless the change is reinforced into systems and culture, it snaps back. These three steps are the skeleton under many later models, Kotter's included.

oneLiner: 自主、胜任、归属三种心理需求被满足，内在动机才真正燃烧。
oneLinerEn: Meet the needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness, and intrinsic motivation truly catches fire.
detail: 德西与瑞安(1985)提出：人有自主(我选择)、胜任(我能行)、归属(我被接纳)三大先天需求，它们被满足时内在动机最强。关键发现是“过度辩护效应”：对本来有趣的活动发金钱奖励，反而把内在兴趣“挤出”。它解释了为什么控制式的胡萝卜大棒常杀鸡取卵，而授权、反馈与团队归属才是长效燃料。
detailEn: Deci and Ryan (1985) held that people have three innate needs — autonomy (I choose), competence (I can) and relatedness (I belong) — and that intrinsic motivation is strongest when they are met. A key finding is the overjustification effect: paying people for an activity they already enjoy can crowd out intrinsic interest. It explains why controlling carrots-and-sticks often backfire while empowerment, feedback and belonging are the lasting fuel.

oneLiner: 察觉与管理自己和他人的情绪，往往是比智商更强的领导力预测项。
oneLinerEn: Perceiving and managing your own and others' emotions is often a better predictor of leadership than IQ.
detail: 萨洛维与梅耶定义、戈尔曼(1995)推广的“情绪智力”：自我觉察、自我管理、社会觉察、关系管理。戈尔曼主张在领导岗位达到一定认知门槛后，情商才是区分卓越与平庸的关键。它广受欢迎，也被批评为概念泛化、易与人格重叠、测量效度存疑——当作可培养的技能有价值，当作万能指标则需谨慎。
detailEn: Salovey and Mayer defined, and Goleman (1995) popularised, 'emotional intelligence': self-awareness, self-management, social awareness and relationship management. Goleman argued that once leaders clear a cognitive threshold, EQ distinguishes the outstanding from the merely adequate. Widely embraced, it is also criticised as conceptually over-broad, overlapping with personality and of contested measurement — valuable as a trainable skill, risky as a do-everything metric.

oneLiner: 目标—现状—选择—意愿：教练不直接给答案，而是用问题带人自己想通。
oneLinerEn: Goal, Reality, Options, Will — the coach withholds answers and questions people into their own clarity.
detail: 亚历山大成形、惠特默推广的 GROW：先澄清要去的 Goal，再看清的 Reality，展开可选的 Options，最后确认行动的 Will。它把管理从“给指令”转向“提好问题”，配合心理安全，让下属自己找到方案并更愿执行。惠特默那句“绩效 = 潜能 − 干扰”是它的精神写照。
detailEn: The GROW model, shaped by Alexander and popularised by Whitmore, moves through Goal (where you want to be), Reality (where you are), Options (what you could do) and Will (what you will do). It turns managing from giving orders into asking good questions and, with psychological safety, lets people find their own answers and own the follow-through. Whitmore's 'performance = potential − interference' captures its spirit.

oneLiner: 培训有没有用分四层看：反应、学习、行为、结果——越往后越难量也越重要。
oneLinerEn: Judge training on four levels — reaction, learning, behaviour, results — the deeper ones harder to measure and more telling.
detail: 唐纳德·柯克帕特里克(1959)的四级：学员喜不喜欢(反应)、学到没有(学习)、回去用不用(行为)、业务有没有改善(结果)。多数培训只量到前两级(现场评分表)，真正决定价值的是行为与结果，却最难归因。它提醒：培训评估要往深处走，否则“掌声雷动”与绩效毫无关系。
detailEn: Donald Kirkpatrick's four levels (1959): did they like it (Reaction), did they learn (Learning), do they apply it back on the job (Behaviour), did the business improve (Results). Most training is measured only at the first two (smile sheets); what decides value — behaviour and results — is hardest to attribute. It urges evaluation to go deeper, lest applause have nothing to do with performance.

oneLiner: 阅读—重述—拆为己用：把书里的知识变成“我自己的下一步行动”，而非止于读完。
oneLinerEn: Read, Interpret, Appropriate — turn a book's idea into 'my own next action' rather than stopping at finishing it.
detail: 赵周在《这样读书就够了》中提出，面向成人“翻转式”学习:R 阅读原文片段、I 用自己的话重述、A 拆为己用(A1 联系过往经验、A2 规划具体可执行的下一步应用)。它针对“读了就忘、用不出来”的痛点，把读书从输入变成行动设计，常与拆书帮、便签法、学习型组织结合。
detailEn: Set out by Zhao Zhou in 'Reading This Way Is Enough' for adult, flipped learning: R (read the original passage), I (interpretation — restate it in your own words), A (appropriation — A1 linking it to past experience, A2 planning a concrete next application). It targets the 'read it, forget it, never use it' problem, turning reading from input into action design, and pairs with book-club facilitation, the sticky-note method and the learning organisation.

oneLiner: 让你激动的不是事件本身，而是你对它的看法——A 触发、B 信念、C 结果。
oneLinerEn: It is not events that upset you but your views of them — Activating event, Belief, Consequence.
detail: 源自阿尔伯特·埃利斯的理性情绪行为疗法:诱发事件(A)并不直接导致情绪与行为后果(C)，中间的信念与解释(B)才是关键;换成更现实、更灵活的信念，情绪随之改变。管理场景中它用于压力与情绪自我管理、非暴力沟通前的“转念”，以及教练式提问。需提醒:它本是心理学工具，用于职场时重在“觉察—辩驳—替换”不合理信念，而非否定真实情绪。
detailEn: From Albert Ellis's rational emotive behaviour therapy: the activating event (A) does not directly cause the emotional and behavioural consequence (C); the intervening belief and interpretation (B) is decisive, and swapping it for a more realistic, flexible one changes how you feel. At work it serves stress and emotion self-management, 'reframing' before nonviolent communication, and coaching questions. A caveat: it is a psychology tool — applied on the job it is about noticing, disputing and replacing irrational beliefs, not denying real feelings.

term: STAR 法则（情境·任务·行动·结果）
oneLiner: 讲一段经历分四步：什么情境、接了什么任务、采取了什么行动、结果如何。
oneLinerEn: Tell an experience in four beats — the Situation, the Task you owned, the Action you took and the Result.
detail: STAR 源于行为面试法，是结构化陈述与述职的通用骨架：先交代背景情境(Situation)，说清要完成的任务或目标(Task)，重点描述自己实际采取的行动(Action)，最后用可衡量的结果(Result)收束。它强迫讲述者少谈空泛态度、多讲具体行为与成效，既能帮应聘者把故事讲清楚，也用于复盘、汇报与写作；常见变体在结果后再补一环反思。
detailEn: STAR comes from behavioural interviewing and is a general skeleton for structured storytelling and reporting: set the background Situation (S), state the Task or goal you owned (T), focus on the concrete Action you took (A), and close with a measurable Result (R). It pushes the speaker away from vague attitudes toward specific behaviour and outcome — useful for candidates telling their story and for reviews, reports and writing; a common variant adds a reflection beat after the result.

oneLiner: 把观点讲成打动人的故事：搭结构、沿时间、亮观点、摆现实、落向往。
oneLinerEn: Turn a point into a story that moves people — Structure, Time-line, Opinion, Reality, then a Yearning to end on.
detail: STORY 是一种把信息组织成叙事的表达框架：S 先搭好结构（开头即抛钩子），T 按时间线交代来龙去脉，O 亮出你的主张与观点，R 呈现支撑观点的现实与细节，Y 以一个唤起向往、指向行动的愿景收尾。它与 SCQA 互补——SCQA 重在把问题讲清、适合商务陈述，STORY 重在用情节与情绪打动人、适合激励、路演与品牌叙事；落点 Y（唤起渴望）正是它区别于纯逻辑表达的关键。
detailEn: STORY organises information as narrative: S builds the structure (open with a hook), T lays out the sequence along time, O states your position and opinion, R shows the reality and detail that back it, and Y closes with a yearning that moves the audience to act. It complements SCQA — SCQA clarifies a problem for business reporting, while STORY persuades through plot and feeling for motivation, pitching and brand narrative; the closing Y (stirring a desire) is what sets it apart from purely logical expression.

oneLiner: 决定优秀绩效的多在水面下：动机、特质、自我形象比可见的技能与知识更关键、也更难改。
oneLinerEn: What drives top performance mostly lies below the surface — motives, traits and self-image matter more than visible skills and knowledge, and are harder to change.
detail: 源自麦克利兰对“卓越者 vs 常人”的研究，由斯宾塞夫妇建模成冰山：水面之上是易见的知识与技能(可培养、易验证)，水面之下是社会角色与自我概念、特质与动机(稳定、难训、却真正区分高下)。它提醒招聘与选拔应看“冰山下的潜力”而非只挑对口专业与证书，培养也要认清越往下越难靠培训改变。胜任力模型由此用于岗位画像、选人、评估与发展；常见方法是行为事件访谈(BEI)，用 STAR 追问具体事例来挖底层特质。
detailEn: From McClelland's studies of outstanding versus average performers, modelled as an iceberg by the Spencers: above the waterline are visible knowledge and skills (trainable, testable); below sit social role and self-concept, traits and motives (stable, hard to teach, yet the true differentiators). It urges hiring to look at below-the-waterline potential rather than the matching major and certificates, and warns that the deeper you go the less training changes it. Competency models built on it serve job profiles, selection, assessment and development, commonly mined by behavioural event interview (BEI) that probes concrete episodes to reveal the underlying traits.

oneLiner: 用“绩效”和“潜力”两轴把人分进九格：谁是顶梁柱、谁是待激活、谁该另谋位置，一目了然。
oneLinerEn: Sort people into nine cells on Performance and Potential — who is a pillar, who to activate, who to move — at a glance.
detail: 九宫格长期被 GE 等用于人才盘点：纵轴是潜力(能否、愿否承担更大更复杂的事)，横轴是过往绩效。右上角“高潜高绩”是接班梯队与重点投资对象，右下角“高绩低潜”是可靠的当前专家、未必适合再升，左上是待验证的新星，双低则需辅导、调岗或退出。价值不在贴标签，而在引发一场“看潜力而非只看业绩”的继任与培养对话。务必警惕它的主观与近因偏差、以及被当作命运判决——潜力该用多种情境证据交叉印证，并定期重估。
detailEn: Long used for talent calibration at GE and elsewhere, the grid plots Potential on one axis (can and will they carry something bigger and more complex) against past Performance on the other. The high-high corner is the successor pool to invest in; the high-performance, low-potential corner are dependable current experts who may not suit another step up; the unproven stars sit opposite; double-low need coaching, redeployment or exit. The value is not the label but the succession-and-development conversation it forces — judging potential, not just results. Beware its subjectivity and recency bias and treating cells as fate; cross-check potential with evidence from several situations and revisit regularly.

oneLiner: 五把钥匙让工作自带动力：技能多样、任务完整、任务重要、自主、反馈。
oneLinerEn: Five keys make a job motivating in itself — skill variety, task identity, task significance, autonomy and feedback.
detail: 哈克曼与奥尔德汉姆提出：工作的五个核心维度——用到的技能是否多样、能否从头做到尾看到整体(任务完整性)、对他人的生活是否真有影响(任务重要性)、有多少自主安排、能否及时得知干得好坏——通过三种心理体验(意义感、责任感、知晓结果)带来内在激励、高绩效与低离职，前提是员工成长需求强、也具备相应能力。它给了“工作再设计”的清单：与其只加工资，不如给整块任务、放手授权、建立反馈闭环；与自我决定理论(自主胜任归属)遥相呼应。
detailEn: Hackman and Oldham held that five core job dimensions — the range of skills used, whether one completes a whole identifiable piece (task identity), whether it truly affects others' lives (task significance), how much discretion one has, and how soon one learns how well it went — work through three psychological states (experienced meaningfulness, responsibility and knowledge of results) to drive intrinsic motivation, high performance and low turnover, provided the worker has growth needs and the ability to match. It hands you a job-redesign checklist: rather than only pay more, give whole tasks, real autonomy and a feedback loop — echoing self-determination theory's autonomy, competence and relatedness.

oneLiner: 按“重要×紧急”分四格:先做重要不紧急的,尽量删掉既不重要又紧急的杂事。
oneLinerEn: Sort tasks on Important by Urgent — do the important-not-urgent first, and drop the busywork that is urgent but not important.
detail: 据美国总统艾森豪威尔的时间观、由柯维推广:“重要”关乎目标与长远,“紧急”关乎当下的催促。四格据此划分:重要且紧急(危机,立即做)、重要不紧急(规划、健身、关系、预防,主动排进去)、紧急不重要(多数打断、某些会议,尽量授权或压缩)、既不重要也不紧急(纯消遣,删)。核心洞见是:人常被紧急牵着走,真正的差别在“为重要不紧急的象限主动腾出时间”,从而减少第一象限的救火。它是个人与团队优先级排程的入口工具。
detailEn: Rooted in Eisenhower's view of time and popularised by Covey: important concerns goals and the long term, urgent concerns what clamours now. The four cells follow — important and urgent (crises, do at once), important not urgent (planning, health, relationships, prevention, schedule them on purpose), urgent not important (most interruptions, some meetings, delegate or compress), and neither (pure diversion, delete). The core insight is that people get bossed around by the urgent, while real leverage lies in deliberately making room for the important-but-not-urgent, cutting today's firefighting. It is the entry tool for prioritising a day or a team's.

oneLiner: 事毕之后四问:本想怎样、实际怎样、为何有差、下次怎么办——把经验炼成能力。
oneLinerEn: After the fact, four questions: what we intended, what happened, why the gap, what next — refining experience into skill.
detail: AAR 源于美军,被联想、华为等引入管理。四个问题(目标、结果、差异原因、可复制与改进)构成极简复盘框架,关键原则是对事不对人、坦诚、及时、留下书面记录,让个人与组织的教训沉淀为标准动作或清单,避免重复踩坑。区别于日常汇报:它专挑“有意的学习”,把成败都当数据,并追问背后的假设。与双环学习、学习型组织、PDCA 相互呼应。
detailEn: Born in the US Army and brought into firms like Lenovo and Huawei, the AAR's four questions — intent, result, cause of the gap, what to keep or fix — form a bare-bones review. Its rules are attack the problem not the person, candour, timeliness and a written record, so lessons harden into standard moves or checklists and mistakes are not repeated. Unlike routine reporting, it deliberately hunts for learning, treats win and loss alike as data, and probes the assumptions behind them. It rhymes with double-loop learning, the learning organisation and PDCA.

oneLiner: 谈事实、说感受、明需求、提请求——把指责式表达换成不评判的沟通。
oneLinerEn: State facts, feeling, need and request — trading accusatory talk for judgment-free communication.
detail: 马歇尔·卢森堡提出的四步:观察(只说我看到的、不夹“你总是/你根本”的评判)、感受(我的情绪而非想法)、需要(背后未被满足的价值)、请求(具体可执行的请求而非命令)。它把冲突从对错之争,转成双方的需求层面。用于绩效反馈、跨部门协作与家庭沟通,能显著降低防御,但需要练习:难点在于分辨“观察与评论、感受与想法”,并且在真实冲突中仍能不带指责地说出需要。
detailEn: Marshall Rosenberg's four steps: observation (what I see, without you-always or you-never judgments), feeling (my emotion, not my thought), need (the unmet value behind it) and request (a concrete ask, not a demand). It turns a conflict from right-versus-wrong into both sides' needs. Used in feedback, cross-team work and family talk, it markedly lowers defensiveness but takes practice: the hard parts are telling observation from evaluation and feeling from thought, and still voicing a need without blame in a real clash.

term: 原则性谈判 (哈佛谈判法)
oneLiner: 对人和气、对事强硬:挖共同利益、用客观标准,而不是比谁嗓门大或谁让步。
oneLinerEn: Soft on the people, hard on the problem: mine shared interests and objective criteria, not volume or concession.
detail: 费舍尔与尤里《Getting to Yes》提出的原则性谈判四要素:把人和问题分开(别让情绪绑架议题)、聚焦利益而非立场(立场背后的真实关切才是解法所在)、先构想共赢的选项、坚持用公平客观标准定价。核心概念是 BATNA——谈判协议的最佳替代方案,你的底气来自“谈崩了还有什么退路”,据此决定何时坚持、何时收手。它也给出“谈判桌上”与“打破僵局”的实操方法,是冲突协作的升级版。
detailEn: Fisher and Ury's Getting to Yes sets out four elements: separate the people from the problem (do not let emotion hijack the issue), focus on interests not positions (the real concern behind a stance is where the cure lies), invent options for mutual gain before deciding, and insist on fair, objective criteria. Its keystone is the BATNA, the best alternative to a negotiated agreement: your backing comes from what you could do if talks fail, telling you when to hold and when to close. It is the upgraded form of conflict and collaboration.

oneLiner: 反馈要说清情境—行为—影响:何时何地、你做了什么、造成什么结果,而非“你这人怎样”。
oneLinerEn: Give feedback as Situation-Behaviour-Impact — when, what you did, what it caused — not what kind of person you are.
detail: SBI 是一种极简结构化反馈:S(情境)锚定具体时间地点,“上周客户会上”;B(行为)描述可观察的行为、不加评判,“你打断了对方三次”;I(影响)说明对我方、项目或客户产生的影响,“客户因此未能讲完顾虑”。因只陈述事实与后果、不给人贴标签,它既能给正面反馈(及时、具体、强化)也能给负面反馈(对事不对人),降低对方防御,更易促成改变。
detailEn: SBI is a bare-bones structured feedback: Situation anchors a specific time and place, Behaviour describes the observable action without judgment, and Impact names the effect on you, the project or the customer. Because it states only fact and consequence and never labels the person, it works for praise (timely, specific, reinforcing) and criticism (problem, not person), lowering defensiveness and enabling change.

oneLiner: 盖洛普用 12 问衡量团队是否“投入”:从“知道要求”到“有人鼓励成长”,越投入越出绩效。
oneLinerEn: Gallup's twelve questions measure whether a team is engaged — from 'I know what is expected' to 'someone encourages growth'.
detail: 盖洛普长期研究发现:敬业度与工作绩效、留任、安全、客户满意相关;它用 12 个层层递进的问题,从基本需求(我是否知道要求、有无材料与工具),到管理支持(意见受重视、被鼓励发展),再到团队归属(伙伴追求卓越)与成长机会(一年内有学习成长)。核心洞见是:敬业度首先由直属经理决定(员工离职多为离开经理而非公司)。与双因素、SDT 不同,它是一个可量化、可对标、可诊断的“温度计”。
detailEn: Gallup's long research links engagement to performance, retention, safety and customer satisfaction, measured by twelve progressive questions from the basics (do I know what is expected, do I have the materials) through manager support (my opinions count, I am encouraged to develop) to belonging and growth (I learn and grow in the past year). The core insight is that engagement is driven chiefly by the direct manager — people quit bosses, not companies. Unlike Herzberg's two factors or self-determination theory, it is a quantifiable, benchmarkable, diagnosable thermometer.

oneLiner: 每个人最深处的职业选择“锚点”不同:技术、管理、自主、安全、创业、服务或挑战。
oneLinerEn: Everyone has a deepest career anchor — technical, managerial, autonomy, security, entrepreneurial, service or challenge.
detail: 施恩基于跟踪毕业生发现:人到一定阶段会形成“职业锚”,即无论如何都不愿放弃的核心价值观与才干,常见八类:技术或功能能力型(追求专业顶尖)、通用管理能力型(追求统筹)、自主或独立型(追求不被约束)、安全或稳定型(追求保障)、创业型(追求创造企业)、服务或献身型(追求使命)、挑战型(追求攻克难题)以及生活平衡型。管理者的意义在于别把专业顶尖的人硬推向其“锚点”之外的管理岗(参见彼得原理)。
detailEn: Schein, tracking graduates, found that people settle on a career anchor — the core values and talent they will not give up — commonly eight types: technical or functional (mastery of a discipline), general managerial (running things), autonomy or independence (not being bound), security or stability (assurance), entrepreneurial (creating ventures), service or dedication (a mission), pure challenge (solving hard problems) and lifestyle balance. The managerial lesson is not to push a technical star into a management post their anchor rejects — a direct tie-in to the Peter principle.

oneLiner: 雇佣关系里那份“没写进合同”的相互期待:一旦违背,失望与疏离先于任何条款。
oneLinerEn: The unwritten mutual expectations of employment — breach them and disappointment and withdrawal come before any clause.
detail: 阿基里斯起、卢梭推广:“心理契约”是员工与组织之间未成文但彼此默认的期待(忠诚换稳定、努力换发展与公平、“听话”换“照看”)。它没有签字、却随时在被“履行”或“违背”:公司裁员、承诺不兑现、“加班无回报”,都会被体验为心理契约破裂,直接侵蚀信任、敬业、组织公民行为,甚至引发离职与报复。管理要点:别过度承诺、坦诚沟通、及早修补;期望对齐是低成本的信任投资。
detailEn: Coined by Argyris and advanced by Rousseau, the psychological contract is the unwritten, mutually assumed expectation between employee and organisation — loyalty for security, effort for development and fairness, deference for being looked after. Signed nowhere yet honoured or breached continuously, layoffs, unmet promises and unpaid overtime are experienced as its violation, eroding trust, engagement and organisational citizenship, even driving exit or retaliation. The managerial rule: do not overpromise, communicate honestly and repair breaches early — aligning expectations is a low-cost investment in trust.
